term.def: Edge AI means running AI on the device itself, like a phone, camera or satellite, instead of sending data to a faraway data centre. It can be faster and use less bandwidth.

prompt.prompt: Act as a strategy advisor. Our team of [team size] works on [business area]. List five decisions where AI could help us this quarter, and the risk to watch for in each.

quiz.q: Myth or Fact: An AI tool always tells you when it is unsure, so a confident answer is a correct answer.
quiz.why: AI tools can sound confident while being wrong. Always check important facts, numbers and names before you use them.

quiz.q: Myth or Fact: A realistic AI-generated image of a person can be made without that person ever posing for a photo.
quiz.why: Image tools can create lifelike pictures from text or from other photos. That is why fake images can spread easily and need checking.

quiz.q: Myth or Fact: Only large tech companies can use AI in their daily work.
quiz.why: Many small firms use AI tools every day for writing, support and analysis. You do not need a big tech team to start.

quiz.q: Myth or Fact: Business Standard reports that two-thirds of MSMEs use AI, but only 21% deploy business software, according to a study.
quiz.why: This restates the Business Standard headline. It suggests many small firms try AI before they adopt wider business software.

quiz.q: Myth or Fact: If you give an AI tool a clearer, more detailed prompt, you usually get a better answer.
quiz.why: AI works from the instructions you give it. Clear context, a goal and a format usually lead to more useful results.
